a.label: Insect
a.def: A small insect, creepy-crawly organism, or mild infectious illness.

b.label: Software bug
b.def: A flaw, error, or failure in computer code that produces incorrect or unintended behavior.

a.label: Cloud
a.def: A visible mass of condensed water vapor floating in the sky.

b.label: Cloud computing
b.def: A global network of remote data centers delivering on-demand computing power, storage, and services over the internet.

a.label: Cookie (biscuit)
a.def: A baked sweet treat, typically flat, round, and crisp or chewy.

b.label: HTTP cookie
b.def: A small text file stored on a user's browser by a website to remember authentication states, settings, or tracking activity.

a.label: Mouse (animal)
a.def: A small, nimble rodent with a pointed snout and long, slender tail.

b.label: Computer mouse
b.def: A handheld peripheral pointing device used to manipulate a visual cursor across a graphical user interface.

a.label: Prompt (punctual)
a.def: Punctual and on time, or an action performed to remind or encourage someone to speak.

b.label: Prompt (AI)
b.def: Natural language input, instruction, or multimodal context provided to a generative model to elicit a specific output.

a.label: Hallucination (perception)
a.def: A psychological or sensory perception of something that is not physically present.

b.label: Hallucination (AI)
b.def: A phenomenon where a generative model outputs confident, grammatically coherent assertions that are factually false, ungrounded, or fabricated.

a.label: Token (coin)
a.def: A physical coin substitute, keepsake, souvenir, or symbolic gesture.

b.label: Token (language model)
b.def: The discrete unit of text (a character, sub-word, or whole word) parsed, processed, and generated by large language models.

a.label: Attention (psychology)
a.def: Concentrated mental focus, awareness, or observational consideration.

b.label: Attention (machine learning)
b.def: A mathematical neural network mechanism that dynamically calculates relevance scores across input sequence components regardless of distance.

a.label: Weight (mass)
a.def: The physical heaviness or gravitational pull exerted on a physical object.

b.label: Weight (neural network)
b.def: A learned numerical parameter within a neural network that determines the relative connection strength between nodes.

a.label: Bias (prejudice)
a.def: Personal prejudice, unfair leaning, or partiality toward a specific perspective.

b.label: Bias (machine learning)
b.def: A fixed mathematical constant added to node inputs to shift activation thresholds, or systematic skewed error present in training datasets.

a.label: Temperature
a.def: The measurable degree of physical heat or coldness in a body or environment.

b.label: Temperature (LLM sampling)
b.def: A hyperparameter controlling the degree of randomness and entropy when sampling probability distributions for token generation.

a.label: Embedding (physical)
a.def: Fixing, wedging, or inserting an object firmly into a surrounding physical substance.

b.label: Embedding (AI)
b.def: The translation of high-dimensional categorical data (words, sentences, images) into dense, continuous numerical vector space.

a.label: Electrical transformer
a.def: An electrical device used to step up or step down alternating voltage between circuits.

b.label: Transformer (deep learning)
b.def: A deep-learning neural network architecture that processes sequences concurrently via self-attention rather than sequential recurrence.

a.label: Model (replica or person)
a.def: A physical miniature replica of an object, or a person employed to display clothing.

b.label: Model (AI)
b.def: A mathematical representation trained on data to recognize patterns, make predictions, or generate novel content.

a.label: Training (athletic)
a.def: Athletic conditioning, exercise routines, or workplace instructional coaching.

b.label: Training (AI)
b.def: The iterative optimization process of adjusting model parameters through optimization algorithms to minimize loss across a dataset.

a.label: Agent (person)
a.def: A real estate broker, talent representative, or covert intelligence operative.

b.label: AI agent
b.def: An autonomous software system designed to perceive its digital environment, reason, invoke tools, and complete sequential goals.

a.label: Pipeline (transport)
a.def: A long physical conduit constructed from connected metal or plastic tubes to transport water, oil, or gas.

b.label: Pipeline (software)
b.def: An automated series of computational data-processing steps where the output of one component serves as the input to the next.

a.label: Architecture (buildings)
a.def: The art, science, and practice of designing physical buildings and habitable structures.

b.label: Software architecture
b.def: The structural design, high-level organization, and interaction patterns among software components, hardware, or neural layers.

a.label: Grounding (punishment or electrical)
a.def: Punishing a child by forbidding them from leaving home, or connecting an electrical circuit to the physical earth.

b.label: Grounding (AI)
b.def: Anchoring an artificial intelligence system's responses to verifiable, external real-world data and facts (e.g., via retrieval systems).

a.label: Alignment (physical)
a.def: Arranging physical items in a straight row or bringing vehicle wheels into parallel position.

b.label: AI alignment
b.def: Steering an AI model's behaviors, objectives, and ethical boundaries to match human values and safety standards.

a.label: Loss (grief or deficit)
a.def: The physical misplacement of an item, financial deficit, or the grief following a death.

b.label: Loss function
b.def: A scalar penalty metric quantifying the distance or discrepancy between an algorithm's prediction and the actual ground-truth label.

a.label: Epoch (era)
a.def: A notable historical era or geological division of planetary time.

b.label: Epoch (machine learning)
b.def: One complete single pass of an entire training dataset through a machine learning model.

a.label: Pruning (gardening)
a.def: Trimming away dead, diseased, or overgrown branches and stems from shrubs or trees.

b.label: Pruning (neural networks)
b.def: Removing redundant, zero-value, or low-impact parameter weights from a trained network to compress memory size and speed inference.

a.label: Distillation (chemistry)
a.def: The process of heating a liquid into vapor and condensing it back into a pure liquid (e.g., spirits, water).

b.label: Knowledge distillation
b.def: Compressing a massive, complex "teacher" neural network into a compact, efficient "student" model by training on the teacher's probability outputs.

a.label: Inference (logic)
a.def: A mental deduction or logical conclusion derived from premises and available evidence.

b.label: Inference (AI)
b.def: The runtime execution phase where a trained model evaluates fresh input to produce a prediction, classification, or text output.

a.label: Thread (yarn)
a.def: A fine strand of twisted cotton, silk, or nylon used in sewing and textile fabrication.

b.label: Thread (computing)
b.def: The smallest standalone sequence of programmed instructions managed independently by an operating system scheduler.

a.label: Fork (utensil)
a.def: A pronged table utensil used for skewering and eating solid food.

b.label: Fork (software)
b.def: Creating a divergent copy of an existing codebase to pursue independent development, or an operating system process duplicating itself.

a.label: Daemon (mythology)
a.def: An attendant mythological spirit, intermediate divinity, or malevolent entity.

b.label: Daemon (computing)
b.def: A background computer program that runs continuously without direct user interactive control, handling system maintenance or service requests.

a.label: Container (box)
a.def: A box, jar, barrel, or large corrugated steel shipping crate used to hold goods.

b.label: Container (software)
b.def: A lightweight, isolated package containing application code together with its exact configuration files, libraries, and binaries.

a.label: Sandbox (play)
a.def: A shallow wooden enclosure filled with sand for children's outdoor recreation.

b.label: Sandbox (computing)
b.def: An isolated, tightly restricted testing environment used to run untrusted or suspect code without risking damage to the host system.

a.label: Memory (mind)
a.def: The cognitive capability of the human mind to retain, recall, and reconstruct past experiences.

b.label: Computer memory
b.def: Physical computer hardware components (such as RAM) utilized for rapid, volatile, short-term data storage while programs execute.

a.label: Stack (pile)
a.def: An orderly vertical pile of dishes, books, firewood, or hay.

b.label: Stack (computing)
b.def: A Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) abstract data structure, or the complete collection of software layers (frameworks, databases, languages) powering an application.

a.label: Queue (line)
a.def: A physical line of people, vehicles, or items awaiting their turn for service.

b.label: Queue (data structure)
b.def: A First-In, First-Out (FIFO) sequential data structure where incoming elements enter at the rear and exit from the front.

a.label: Cache (hidden store)
a.def: A hidden stash or concealed reserve of weapons, ammunition, or supplies.

b.label: Cache (computing)
b.def: A high-speed hardware or software storage mechanism storing temporary data copies to reduce latency on repeated requests.

a.label: Driver (person)
a.def: The human operator seated behind the steering controls of a motorized vehicle.

b.label: Device driver
b.def: A specialized software component facilitating direct communication between an operating system and connected hardware devices.

a.label: Port (harbor)
a.def: A coastal harbor town or protected maritime dock for cargo and passenger vessels.

b.label: Port (networking)
b.def: A logical software communication endpoint identified by an integer number, or a physical hardware interface socket on a device.

a.label: Virus (biology)
a.def: A microscopic biological pathogen that replicates inside living host cells, causing illness.

b.label: Computer virus
b.def: Self-replicating computer code designed to spread across digital devices by modifying existing host programs and inserting its payload.

a.label: Worm (animal)
a.def: A soft, limbless, burrowing invertebrate crawling through soil.

b.label: Computer worm
b.def: A standalone malicious program that actively spreads copies of itself across computer networks without requiring human activation or host files.

a.label: Trojan (Troy)
a.def: A historical citizen or defender of the ancient Bronze Age city of Troy.

b.label: Trojan horse (malware)
b.def: Malware intentionally masquerading as benign, useful utility software to trick a user into downloading and executing it.

a.label: Patch (fabric)
a.def: A scrap of fabric sewn over a tear or worn area in clothing.

b.label: Patch (computing)
b.def: A piece of supplementary code applied to software to fix security vulnerabilities, eliminate bugs, or add features.

a.label: Boot (footwear)
a.def: A sturdy style of footwear encasing the foot and reaching up the calf or ankle.

b.label: Booting
b.def: The operational process of loading and initializing an operating system kernel from persistent storage into active memory.

a.label: Crash (collision)
a.def: A sudden, violent physical impact or vehicular collision accompanied by a loud noise.

b.label: Crash (computing)
b.def: An abrupt, unplanned software shutdown or operating system halt caused by an unhandled system failure.

a.label: Ping (sound or sonar)
a.def: A short, sharp metallic sound, or a solitary high-frequency acoustic pulse emitted by a submarine sonar.

b.label: Ping (networking)
b.def: An ICMP network diagnostic utility sent to an IP address to determine reachability and measure round-trip response time.

a.label: Mirror
a.def: A polished, reflective glass surface showing an optical reflection of whoever faces it.

b.label: Mirror (computing)
b.def: An exact, synchronized secondary server or website copy maintained to distribute bandwidth loads and safeguard file availability.

a.label: Root (botany)
a.def: The descending underground organ of a plant that anchors it and absorbs moisture and minerals.

b.label: Root (computing)
b.def: The foundational, topmost tier in a hierarchical filesystem, or the administrative superuser account wielding full system control.

a.label: Branch (tree)
a.def: A woody structural division extending outward from the main trunk of a tree.

b.label: Branch (version control)
b.def: An independent line of software modification created within a version control repository without affecting the central base.

a.label: Trunk (tree or elephant)
a.def: The thick primary wooden stem of a mature tree, or an elephant's elongated prehensile nose.

b.label: Trunk (version control)
b.def: The authoritative, central, stable branch of code in version control systems, from which subsidiary branches split off.

a.label: Commit (pledge)
a.def: Pledging oneself morally to a serious long-term relationship, duty, or obligation.

b.label: Commit (version control)
b.def: Recording and cementing a verified set of source code changes into the persistent timeline of a version control system.

a.label: Push (physical)
a.def: Exerting physical force away from oneself against an object to move it forward.

b.label: Push (version control)
b.def: Uploading and transferring locally staged commits from a personal computer to an upstream remote repository.

a.label: Pull (physical)
a.def: Exerting physical force inward toward oneself to bring an object closer.

b.label: Pull (version control)
b.def: Fetching the most recent changes from an upstream remote repository and merging them into the active local workspace.

a.label: Hash (food)
a.def: A traditional breakfast dish of chopped potatoes, meat, and onions browned in a frying pan.

b.label: Hash function
b.def: A deterministic mathematical transformation that converts an arbitrary block of data into a fixed-size alphanumeric string.

a.label: Socket (outlet or anatomy)
a.def: An electrical wall outlet or a skeletal cavity designed to receive an articulating bone end.

b.label: Network socket
b.def: A bidirectional software endpoint bound to an IP address and port that facilitates inter-process network messaging.

a.label: Protocol (diplomacy)
a.def: Formal diplomatic etiquette, ceremonial rules, and code of conduct governing state affairs.

b.label: Communication protocol
b.def: A standardized, rigid specification of syntactical and procedural rules governing digital data transmission between devices.

a.label: Shell (casing)
a.def: The rigid, calcified outer protective casing enclosing a turtle, mollusk, or avian egg.

b.label: Shell (computing)
b.def: A command-line or visual interpreter exposing operating system kernel capabilities to human users and scripts.

a.label: Terminal (transport)
a.def: The final destination building at the conclusion of an airport runway, rail line, or bus route.

b.label: Computer terminal
b.def: An electronic interface or terminal-emulator application accepting character inputs to execute commands and output textual data.

a.label: Window
a.def: A transparent glass opening framed in a building or vehicle wall to admit light and air.

b.label: Window (computing)
b.def: A bounded, rectangular visual display partition presenting the interface and controls of a distinct computer application.

a.label: Monitor (supervisor)
a.def: A student appointed to oversee hall conduct, or a supervisor assigned to observe an exam.

b.label: Computer monitor
b.def: An electronic visual output panel displaying graphics, video, and text processed by a computer's GPU.

a.label: Key (lock)
a.def: A carved, notched piece of brass or iron turned within a lock cylinder to throw a bolt.

b.label: Key (cryptography)
b.def: A variable piece of alphanumeric data or algorithmic value used to encrypt, decrypt, or validate data, or identify values in databases.

a.label: Lock (security device)
a.def: A mechanical fastening mechanism secured with a deadbolt, padlock, or combination tumbler.

b.label: Lock (computer science)
b.def: A synchronization primitive that restricts shared memory or resource access to a single processing thread at a time.

a.label: Salt (seasoning)
a.def: White crystalline sodium chloride mineral extracted from seawater or mines to season food.

b.label: Salt (cryptography)
b.def: Randomly generated bits appended to plaintext passwords before running them through a cryptographic hash to prevent rainbow table attacks.

a.label: Seed (botany)
a.def: The reproductive unit of a flowering plant capable of developing into an identical plant.

b.label: Random seed
b.def: An initial baseline value supplied to a pseudorandom number generator algorithm to initialize its predictable output sequence.

a.label: Bus (vehicle)
a.def: A large motorized passenger vehicle operating on public thoroughfares along predetermined urban routes.

b.label: Bus (computing)
b.def: A physical communication system and set of wire pathways moving data and power between computer subsystems.

a.label: Host (person)
a.def: A welcoming party organizer entertaining invited guests in their home or restaurant.

b.label: Host (network)
b.def: A network-connected computer hardware device or server providing services, data, or network interfaces to remote nodes.

a.label: Client (customer)
a.def: An individual or enterprise paying a professional practitioner (such as an attorney or architect) for tailored services.

b.label: Client (computing)
b.def: A piece of hardware or client-side software program requesting services, assets, or data from a central server.

a.label: Server (food service)
a.def: A food-service worker carrying trays to restaurant tables, or a tennis player putting a ball into play.

b.label: Server (computing)
b.def: A persistent central software daemon or dedicated computer machine responding to requests over a network from clients.

a.label: Cluster (group)
a.def: A dense physical grouping or bunch of berries, stars, or flowers gathered closely together.

b.label: Computer cluster
b.def: A group of loosely or tightly connected computers that coordinate tasks over a network to function as a singular high-performance machine.

a.label: Farm
a.def: An expanse of cultivated rural land and barns dedicated to growing agricultural crops or rearing livestock.

b.label: Server farm
b.def: A massive collection of computer servers co-located in a dedicated facility to handle colossal computational and storage loads.

a.label: Leech (animal)
a.def: An aquatic or terrestrial bloodsucking annelid worm formerly used in traditional medical bloodletting.

b.label: Leech (computing)
b.def: A peer-to-peer file sharing participant who downloads data without uploading or seeding equivalent chunks back to the swarm.

a.label: Lurk (linger)
a.def: Lingering furtively, covertly, or inconspicuously in shadowy areas with sinister intent.

b.label: Lurker (online)
b.def: Reading, monitoring, and consuming discussions on digital forums, chatrooms, or social platforms without ever posting or contributing.

a.label: Troll (folklore)
a.def: An ugly, hostile mythical giant or dwarf residing under bridges or inside subterranean caverns.

b.label: Internet troll
b.def: A provocateur who posts intentionally inflammatory, disruptive, or nonsensical messages online to bait outrage and distress.

a.label: Flame (fire)
a.def: The glowing, visible, hot tongue of combustion rising from burning wood or gas.

b.label: Flaming (internet)
b.def: A blistering, hostile, and direct personal attack or string of insults launched against another user in an online community.

a.label: Spam (food)
a.def: A commercial brand of canned, precooked pink meat made primarily of chopped pork shoulder and ham.

b.label: Spam (electronic)
b.def: Irrelevant, unwanted, and identical electronic messages blasted in bulk across email, direct messages, and comments.

a.label: Fishing
a.def: The leisure sport or livelihood of catching water-dwelling vertebrates using bait, hooks, or nets.

b.label: Phishing
b.def: A deceptive social-engineering attack where malicious actors impersonate trusted institutions to steal private passwords and account credentials.

a.label: Bot (robot)
a.def: Shortened colloquial shorthand for a physical, metallic science-fiction robot or mechanical android.

b.label: Bot (software)
b.def: An automated software program executing repetitive, scheduled tasks and scripts over the web faster than humans can.

a.label: Scrape (abrasion)
a.def: Rubbing an abrasive surface across skin to produce an abrasion or cleaning grease off a skillet.

b.label: Web scraping
b.def: The programmatic extraction and parsing of raw data and content directly from public-facing websites.

a.label: Crawl (movement)
a.def: Moving forward slowly across a flat surface on hands and knees or on one's belly.

b.label: Web crawl
b.def: The automated, systematic traversal of hyperlinks across the internet by search engine software to index web pages.

a.label: Spider (arachnid)
a.def: An eight-legged predatory arachnid with fangs, spinnerets, and silk-producing abdominal organs.

b.label: Spider (web crawler)
b.def: A specialized search engine bot dispatched to traverse internet sites and harvest data for indexing.

a.label: Spider web
a.def: A delicate, geometric network of sticky silk threads constructed by spiders to ensnare insects.

b.label: World Wide Web
b.def: The World Wide Web; an interconnected system of hyperlinked public pages accessible via the internet through HTTP protocols.

a.label: Net (mesh)
a.def: A meshed textile fabric manufactured from looped, knotted cord used for trapping fish, game, or tennis balls.

b.label: The Net (internet)
b.def: Shorthand for the global internet infrastructure connecting billions of computing nodes together.

a.label: Traffic (vehicles)
a.def: Congestion and movement of motor vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians traveling along urban roads.

b.label: Network traffic
b.def: The volumetric flow of transmitted digital data packets and visitor communications traveling across network links.

a.label: Bandwidth (signal or personal)
a.def: The width of an electromagnetic frequency band, or colloquial human capacity to tolerate mental stress and tasks.

b.label: Bandwidth (networking)
b.def: The maximum volumetric data-carrying capacity and transmission rate of a network connection measured in bits per second.

a.label: Footprint
a.def: An indentation or impression left by an animal's paw or human boot on soft earth, sand, or snow.

b.label: Memory footprint
b.def: The overall physical or digital resource overhead (storage size, RAM utilization, CPU cycles) consumed by a running program.

a.label: Garbage (waste)
a.def: Decomposing food waste, domestic refuse, and disposable detritus discarded into bins.

b.label: Garbage (computer science)
b.def: Objects and blocks of system memory that were dynamically allocated by code but are no longer accessible or referenced.

a.label: Dump (landfill)
a.def: A municipal landfill site where industrial and household refuse is discarded and buried.

b.label: Core dump
b.def: A raw, diagnostic snapshot of memory contents (core dump) or database structure written to disk during a crash or backup.

a.label: Leak (fluid)
a.def: A perforation or hairline fracture through which water, fuel, or gas escapes from a pipe.

b.label: Memory leak
b.def: A program bug where dynamic memory, sockets, or file handles remain reserved and unreleased, degrading available system resources over time.

a.label: Spill (liquid)
a.def: An accidental knocking over of a drinking glass, slopping liquid across a tabletop or carpet.

b.label: Register spill
b.def: An event where a compiler exhausts its high-speed processor registers and is forced to dump register variables into slower RAM.

a.label: Overflow (liquid)
a.def: Liquid pouring uncontrollably over the rim of an overfilled bathtub or swollen riverbank.

b.label: Overflow (computing)
b.def: An error occurring when a computational value exceeds the maximum numeric threshold supported by its allocated memory buffer.

a.label: Exception (special case)
a.def: A special case or individual circumstance expressly exempt from an established law or general principle.

b.label: Exception (programming)
b.def: An anomalous condition or runtime disruption encountered during software execution requiring immediate special handling.

a.label: Catch (sport)
a.def: Intercepting and securing a flying baseball or thrown object with one's outstretched hand.

b.label: Catch (programming)
b.def: A programming construct written to intercept, suppress, or resolve an exception condition thrown by a block of code.

a.label: Throw (physical)
a.def: Propelling an object through the air by rapid forward movement of the arm and hand.

b.label: Throw (programming)
b.def: Explicitly raising an exception or error flag to transfer programmatic execution flow directly to a designated error-handling block.

a.label: Tree
a.def: A tall woody perennial plant featuring an upright solitary trunk supporting branches and foliage.

b.label: Tree (data structure)
b.def: A hierarchical, non-linear linked data structure composed of a root node, child branches, and leaf endpoints without cycles.

a.label: Forest
a.def: A sprawling terrestrial ecosystem dominated by thousands of closely spaced mature trees and undergrowth.

b.label: Random forest
b.def: An ensemble collection of disjoint decision trees whose individual classifications are aggregated to formulate a stronger prediction (Random Forest).

a.label: Stream (water)
a.def: A natural, narrow, flowing body of fresh water meandering over rocks between small banks.

b.label: Stream (computing)
b.def: A continuous, sequential transmission of data chunks piped and processed incrementally without buffering the entire payload at once.

a.label: Feed (animal)
a.def: Providing grain, hay, or nourishment to domestic livestock and barn animals.

b.label: News feed
b.def: An algorithmically updated, scrolling content stream supplying chronological articles, images, or updates to a user interface.

a.label: Wall
a.def: A vertical, solid brick, plaster, or stone structural partition demarcating or enclosing a room.

b.label: Wall (Facebook)
b.def: A dedicated public message board space on a social media profile where other accounts publish text and media.

a.label: Profile (silhouette)
a.def: An outline, silhouette, or drawing depicting a person's head and features viewed from the side.

b.label: User profile
b.def: A digital summary record cataloging an individual user's account preferences, bio, identity credentials, and history.

a.label: Handle (grip)
a.def: The physical protrusion, knob, or bar on a utensil or door engineered to be grasped by a human palm.

b.label: Handle (username)
b.def: A designated screen name, alias, or unique public username (or in low-level code, an opaque token referencing an OS resource).

a.label: Ghost (spirit)
a.def: The disembodied, terrifying apparition or wandering spirit of a deceased person.

b.label: Ghost (disk imaging and ghosting)
b.def: Sector-by-sector cloning of an entire storage disk into a unified image file, or suddenly severing online communication without an exit.

a.label: Brick
a.def: A hardened, kiln-fired rectangular block of clay used for masonry, chimney building, and paving.

b.label: Brick (electronics)
b.def: A consumer electronic gadget ruined and rendered wholly inert by corrupted firmware, turning it into a useless paperweight.

a.label: Zombie (folklore)
a.def: An undead, reanimated, mindless corpse driven by supernatural reanimation or contagion in folklore.

b.label: Zombie (computing)
b.def: A compromised internet-connected computer silently co-opted by a malicious controller to participate in distributed botnet attacks.

a.label: Beacon (signal fire)
a.def: A tall signal fire lit on a hilltop or a coastal lighthouse beam guiding ships through fog.

b.label: Bluetooth beacon
b.def: A Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) hardware transmitter broadcasting periodic proximity signals to nearby mobile devices.

a.label: Breadcrumb (bread)
a.def: A tiny morsel of dry bread flaked off a loaf or scattered to mark a trail.

b.label: Breadcrumb navigation
b.def: A horizontal navigation trail displaying a user's location hierarchy within a website (e.g., Home > Hardware > Monitors).

a.label: Canary (bird)
a.def: A small yellow songbird historically carried into underground coal mines to detect lethal carbon monoxide leaks.

b.label: Canary release
b.def: Deploying software updates to a tiny, isolated percentage of live infrastructure to detect regressions before a full rollout.

a.label: Carousel (ride)
a.def: An amusement park merry-go-round with carved wooden horses revolving around a central mechanical axis.

b.label: Carousel (UI)
b.def: A cyclical slideshow component that rotates horizontally through banners, cards, or featured content blocks.

a.label: Chip (snack or splinter)
a.def: A thin, crunchy slice of fried potato snack, or a splinter flaked off wood or stone.

b.label: Integrated circuit
b.def: An integrated circuit (IC) fabricated on a micro-scale semiconductor wafer containing billions of etched transistors.

a.label: Class (school or society)
a.def: A group of students gathered for academic instruction, or a socioeconomic tier in human society.

b.label: Class (programming)
b.def: An extensible code blueprint defining the default properties, state fields, and executable methods for instantiated objects.

a.label: Clipboard (board)
a.def: A stiff board with a spring-loaded metal clip at the top used to hold loose paperwork for writing.

b.label: Clipboard (computing)
b.def: An operating system memory buffer holding copied or cut text, media, and files awaiting a paste command.

a.label: Clone (biology)
a.def: An organism produced asexually from an existing ancestor with genetically identical DNA.

b.label: Clone (Git)
b.def: Downloading an identical, fully operational copy of a remote source repository onto a local workstation.

a.label: Core (center)
a.def: The central seed-bearing fibrous interior of an apple, or Earth's molten nickel-iron center.

b.label: Core (CPU)
b.def: An independent physical computational engine inside a CPU capable of reading and executing thread instructions.

a.label: Cursor (slide rule)
a.def: The clear, sliding runner pane on a mathematical slide rule used to align calculation markings.

b.label: Cursor (user interface)
b.def: An on-screen visual indicator (arrow, hand, or blinking bar) indicating where user input or mouse interaction will land.

a.label: Deadlock (standoff)
a.def: An impassable political or contractual standoff where neither party will budge, stalling progress entirely.

b.label: Deadlock (computing)
b.def: A concurrency bug where two or more threads freeze permanently because each holds a lock the other requires.

a.label: Decay (rot)
a.def: The biological rot and decomposition of organic matter broken down by bacteria and fungi.

b.label: Weight decay
b.def: A regularization penalty (e.g., weight decay) that shrinks parameter values during training to prevent overfitting.

a.label: Desktop (furniture)
a.def: The flat, polished wooden writing surface resting on top of a piece of study furniture.

b.label: Desktop (GUI)
b.def: The primary base graphical user interface displaying system icons, taskbars, and application windows.

a.label: Directory (listing)
